name: Serverless Application
description: A pattern for building applications using managed serverless compute services where the cloud provider handles all infrastructure provisioning, scaling, and maintenance. Functions execute in response to events and scale to zero when idle, providing a pay-per-use cost model.
whenToUse: Event-driven workloads with variable or unpredictable traffic patterns
Applications that benefit from automatic scaling to zero during idle periods
Small teams wanting to minimise operational overhead and infrastructure management
API backends, data processing pipelines, and automation tasks
Prototyping and MVP development where speed to market is prioritised
whenNotToUse: Long-running processes exceeding function timeout limits (typically 15 minutes)
Workloads requiring persistent connections (WebSockets, long-polling) without additional services
Applications with consistent high-throughput where reserved compute is more cost-effective
Workloads with strict cold-start latency requirements for every request
Complex stateful applications that require local filesystem or in-memory state

typicalComponents.name: Function Compute
typicalComponents.purpose: Execute business logic in response to events without managing servers
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, or Cloud Functions

typicalComponents.name: API Gateway
typicalComponents.purpose: Expose functions as HTTP endpoints with authentication and throttling
typicalComponents.technology: API Gateway, Azure API Management, or Cloud Endpoints

typicalComponents.name: Event Sources
typicalComponents.purpose: Trigger function execution from queues, streams, schedules, or HTTP requests

typicalComponents.name: Managed Database
typicalComponents.purpose: Store application data in a serverless-compatible database

typicalComponents.name: Step Functions/Workflows
typicalComponents.purpose: Orchestrate multi-step serverless workflows with error handling
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Step Functions, Azure Durable Functions, or Cloud Workflows

securityControls: Apply least-privilege IAM roles to each function with minimal permissions
Encrypt environment variables and use secrets manager for sensitive configuration
Validate all input events before processing to prevent injection attacks
Implement function-level concurrency limits to prevent runaway execution
Enable VPC integration for functions accessing private resources
Implement request signing and API key validation at the gateway layer
resilienceConsiderations: Serverless platforms provide inherent high availability across multiple AZs
Automatic retry behaviour for asynchronous invocations with DLQ for failures
Stateless functions are inherently resilient — failed instances are replaced automatically
Implement idempotent function logic to handle duplicate invocations safely
Use step functions for complex workflows to manage state and handle partial failures
Cold starts may impact latency — use provisioned concurrency for latency-sensitive paths
costConsiderations: Pay-per-invocation model — zero cost when idle, scales linearly with usage
Extremely cost-effective for sporadic or low-traffic workloads
High-throughput sustained workloads may be cheaper on reserved containers
Monitor function duration and memory allocation to optimise per-invocation costs
API Gateway request costs add to overall expense at high volumes
Factor in the cost of associated services (databases, queues, storage)
operationalConsiderations: No server patching or OS maintenance required
Monitoring focuses on function errors, duration, throttling, and cold starts
Distributed tracing essential for debugging multi-function workflows
Deployment automation needed for managing many individual functions
Local development and testing requires emulation tools or cloud-based testing
Vendor lock-in considerations — function code is portable but integrations are not

questionsToAsk: What is the expected invocation frequency and traffic pattern?
Are there latency requirements that cold starts would violate?
What is the maximum execution duration for the longest-running operation?
Does the application require persistent connections or local state?
What event sources will trigger function execution?
Is the team comfortable with serverless debugging and observability tooling?
commonMistakes: Building monolithic functions instead of small, focused, single-purpose functions
Not implementing proper error handling and dead letter queues for async invocations
Ignoring cold start impact on user-facing latency-sensitive endpoints
Over-provisioning function memory without measuring actual requirements
Not implementing distributed tracing, making debugging multi-function flows impossible
